title: ApplicationView
description: A registered OAuth client as the administrative surface sees it, derived from identity_application::applications::ApplicationView. The self-service view of the same application is a NARROWER projection (contracts/self-service/v1/connected-application.schema.json), and the difference is deliberate: a browser that does not need the registered redirect URIs and scopes should not be handed them.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; no registration command has a body

application_id.description: The application's identifier. A transparent UUID newtype in Rust.

client_id.description: The PUBLIC client_id. It appears in browser redirects by design, so it is not a secret. Unique across all applications, enforced by the applications.client_id unique index — 191 bytes because that index key must fit the D1 index limit alongside its collation.

display_name.description: The display name, shown in the admin UI and on the consent screen.

status.description: Whether it may be used. active is the only status that permits authorization (ApplicationStatus::permits_authorization). retired is ONE-WAY — an abandoned integration cannot be woken up years later by a stale automation — and that is why retired is distinct from suspended rather than a suspended with a longer timeout.

access_mode.description: Which access mode it registered under. Both modes require PKCE unconditionally (ApplicationAccessMode::requires_pkce), deliberately: the IETF is moving the ecosystem toward mandatory PKCE for public clients, and making it optional here would mean a future tightening is a breaking change to stored registrations rather than a config flip.

redirect_uris.description: Its registered redirect URIs, PRE-REGISTERED. A redirect URI is never learned from a request at runtime — a redirect target learned at request time is the open redirect this design refuses. Each must be absolute, http or https, and fragment-free, at most 2048 bytes; the domain model refuses the rest.
redirect_uris.x-matching-rule: Application::allows_redirect_uri compares EXACTLY. Never a prefix, never a glob, never normalised. Phase 5's exit condition requires that there be no prefix, wildcard or normalisation escape.

allowed_scopes.description: Its registered scopes, pre-registered at registration. A request for a scope outside this set is refused, and a grant is narrowed to the intersection of what was asked and what is registered.

secret_rotated_at_ms.description: When its secret was last rotated, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Null means NEVER — which for a confidential client is a FINDING, not a neutral state. Serialised as null, not omitted.
secret_rotated_at_ms.x-serde-note: Option<i64> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present.

x-what-this-view-never-contains.client_secret: never, in any read. A secret is returned exactly once by the registration or rotation call that mints it and is not retrievable afterwards. RegisterApplicationOutcome's hand-written Debug prints "<redacted>" for it, and ClientSecret has no Debug derive at all, so `{:?}` on one is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a silent leak.

x-phase: Phase 4 — OIDC provider (client registration and the confidential/public distinction); Phase 5 — Applications, grants, and the self-service surface for the console screen that renders it
